source_text: Si quis dicit corpus Christi increatum, et non confitetur ipsum increatum Deum Verbum ex creata humanitate incarnationem ostendisse, factumque esse hominem sicut scriptum est, anathema sit. Quomodo enim corpus increatum dici potest? Nam quod increatum est, etiam passionis expers est, et neque vulnerari neque attrectari potest. Christus autem a mortuis resurgens clavorum et vulnerationem lancea factam corpusque suum palpandum discipulis demonstrans clausis ianuis ingressus est. Sed ut divinitatis opera et corporis veritatem ostenderet: et cum alioqui Deus esset, homo agnoscebatur; et cum esset vere homo, Deus tamen ex suis operibus ostendebatur.
thought_title: The created body of Christ shown by his passion and resurrection
orientation: Gregory opens his treatise by anathematizing anyone who says Christ's body is uncreated, then argues that the risen Christ's wounds and touchable body prove it was created.
pass_a_gloss: If anyone says [the] body of Christ [is] uncreated, and does not confess [that] he himself, [the] uncreated God [the] Word, showed [his] incarnation from created humanity, and [that he] was made man as it is written, let him be anathema. For how can [the] body be said [to be] uncreated? For that which is uncreated is also incapable of suffering, and can neither be wounded nor be touched. But Christ, rising from [the] dead, showing [the] nails and [the] wound made by [the] lance and his body to be touched to [the] disciples, entered through closed doors. But [he did this] so that he might show [the] works of [the] divinity and [the] truth of [the] body: and although he was otherwise God, he was recognized [as] man; and although he was truly man, God nevertheless was shown from his own works.

choices.why: Fixed glossary term; preserves the technical sense of having no beginning and being incapable of suffering.
Fixed glossary rendering; keeps the full sense of being unable to undergo passion.
Fixed glossary formula; retains the liturgical condemnation force.
Literal rendering preserves the resurrection detail of passing through locked doors.
rejected: came in when the doors were shut
entered though the doors were locked

choices.why: Keeps the concessive force and the sense that in all other respects he was God.
rejected: though he was God in other respects

pass_b_english: If anyone says that the body of Christ is uncreated, and does not confess that the uncreated God the Word himself displayed his incarnation from created humanity and became man as it is written, let him be anathema. For how can a body be called uncreated? What is uncreated is also incapable of suffering, and can be neither wounded nor touched. But Christ, rising from the dead, showed the disciples the marks of the nails and the wound made by the lance, and his body able to be touched, and he entered through closed doors. He did this to display both the works of his divinity and the reality of his body: although he was otherwise God, he was recognized as man; and although he was truly man, God was nevertheless demonstrated from his own works.

last_rejected.why: 'otherwise' misrenders 'alioqui' (otherwise/in other respects/else); here 'alioqui' means 'in other respects' or 'for the rest,' not 'otherwise' in the sense of 'on the other hand.' The sense is 'since he was God in other respects' or 'as he was otherwise God.' But 'otherwise God' is awkward and potentially misleading—suggesting he was God in a different mode.
last_rejected.fix: since he was for the rest God, he was recognized as man
last_rejected.ruling: 'otherwise' is a standard sense of 'alioqui'; rendering within normal range, not a meaning change.
